BY ADV GOVERNMENT PLEADER  THIS CROSS OBJECTION/CROSS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 09.07.2025, ALONG WITH WA.2495/2015, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 WA No.2495/2015, CO No.210/2015  5  2025:KER:50843  JUDGMENT SUSHRUT ARVIND DHARMADHIKARI,J
None appears for the respondents.

2. The present intra-court appeal filed under Section 5 of the Kerala High Court Act, 1958 assails the Judgment dated 13.10.2015 passed in WP(C) No.30005/2015 (A), whereby the learned Single Judge has allowed the Writ Petition quashing Ext.P1 order with liberty to the appellants.
Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellants submitted that during pendency of the appeal, the respondent's proprietorship concern has been sold to someone else and he is operating the firm.
He further pointed out that the learned Single Judge in point no.ii, paragraph ii.e. has granted the following liberty.

"ii.e. In this case, this Court is of the view that there are clear findings that the petitioner's products are sub-standard, thus, after giving one more opportunity to the petitioner to comply with the standards, the Commissioner is free to take such measures to put public at alert about sub-standard products sold by the petitioner or to cancel the licence under Section 32(3) of the FSS Act."
3.

He contends that the ownership of the respondent firm already stood transferred and in view of the liberty and also due to efflux of time, no action is required to be taken against the respondent at present.
However, the appellants are monitoring the firm as per law.
In view of the aforesaid statement, this Court finds no reason to interfere with the judgment passed by the learned Single Judge.
Accordingly, the WA No.2495/2015, CO No.210/2015 2025:KER:50843 Writ Appeal is disposed of.
So far as CO. No. 210/2015 filed by the 1 st respondent is concerned, there is no provision under the Rules to file such a Cross Objection.
Therefore, the same is not maintainable and is rejected.
